messages:
sam: :rotating_light: Acme (acme-eng) opened a ticket — theyre getting lots of 429s across eu-west-1 since ~16:05 UTC. They report request spikes and customer impact. Posting logs they captured.

acme-eng: yes, sorry for the noise. We pushed a client change that altered batching/retry behavior. Saw sharp parallelism at top-of-minute. Example pattern: many small requests from 100+ containers syncing every minute.

elaine: thanks for the quick context. @tony can you look at the ratecap side? Ill grab traces and x-request-ids from the customer.

tony: on it. first glance from metrics: their per-minute RPM and per-minute tokens (TPM) hit the configured cap for 3 contiguous minutes, then partial relief. Routing stayed in eu-west-1. No global fallback triggered.

sam: sending the sample header they included:

```
x-request-id: acme-req-20260317-42
x-region: eu-west-1
user-agent: acme-sync/2.3.1
content-length: 234
```

ops-bot: Alert: rate_limit_violation detected for tenant acme-corp, windows: rpm=600/600, tpm=12000/12000, affected AZs: eu-west-1a/eu-west-1b. (automated)

elaine: quick checklist for triage:
- confirm if client aligned to minute boundary (spikes at 0s)
- check SDK keepalive/multiplexing
- inspect retry jitter/backoff config
- decide on temporary quota bump vs client fix

acme-eng: we do see our jobs synchronize at minute boundaries. Retries are immediate with exponential backoff but initial burst is large.

tony: that matches. Two likely vectors: coordinated top-of-minute bursts (thundering herd) or a retry storm from transient 429s. Can you share a short recording of request timing distribution? even CSV of timestamps helps.

acme-eng: attaching a trimmed log segment (timestamps in ms). We see ~8k requests in 30s from their fleet.

sam: ok. mitigation options in order of speed:
1) temporary per-tenant quota bump for 30m while they roll client fix
2) enable per-route burst smoothing (we can gate their highest-volume endpoint)
3) advise the customer to add random jitter to scheduled jobs and add concurrency cap in client

elaine: for a safe immediate step I recommend a small token bump + enable our auto-throttling policy for the tenant to smooth peaks. Tony, can you run a 30m bump + enable auto-throttle and monitor indicators? If its still thrashing, we rollback bump and escalate.

tony: running bump now. ETA 30s. also enabled tenant-level smoothing: token window smoothing=enabled, max-burst-factor=1.5. keeping logs open.

support-bot: Action logged: quota.bump applied for tenant acme-corp (+20% rpm, +10% tpm) by tony. smoothing policy toggled.

acme-eng: thanks team, were seeing error rate drop already. Big help. Well roll a client patch to add jitter and limit parallel workers next deploy.

sam: follow-up TODOs:
- acme to deploy client jitter + concurrency cap (owner: acme-eng)
- support to keep bump for 30 minutes then expire (owner: tony)
- ops to check SLO indicators for any regressions (owner: elaine)

elaine: leaving a short repro guide here for postmortem (ask customer for confirmation):
- set up 120 container workers
- schedule sync at the top of each minute
- no jitter, initial retry attempt immediate
- observe RPM/TPM climb and 429s within 10-20s

acme-eng: will confirm and share the patch timestamp. appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup:

sam: closing the thread when the bump expires and customer confirms fix. Marking as high priority incident->support handoff.
